Location A (172.16.10.x, 172.16.20.x) at all. Other zones can
still reach each other. Find what isolated Location C.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router4 uplinks eth5 (-> router3,
  172.25.1.0/24) AND eth4 (-> router5, 192.168.15.0/24)
Mechanism: router4 (Location C's edge) is DUAL-HOMED to the rest
  of the network -- via router3 over 172.25.1.0/24 (eth5) AND via
  router5 over 192.168.15.0/24 (eth4). Cutting only one uplink
  reroutes over the other with no outage, so BOTH must be down to
  isolate Location C. With both down, RIP withdraws every path and
  Location C loses Locations A and B.
Localization: router4 (both uplinks, eth5 and eth4)
Root cause: both of router4's upstream links are down
  (eth5 -> router3 and eth4 -> router5)
Fix: `ip link set eth5 up; ip link set eth4 up` on router4
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth5 up; ip link set eth4 up` on router4

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Both uplink interfaces on router4 — eth4 (192.168.15.2/24, the link to router5 on the link_r4_r5 segment) and eth5 (172.25.1.1/24, the link to router3 on the link_r4_r3 segment) — are in kernel state DOWN.

**Mechanism:** Router4 is the sole Layer-3 gateway for Location C (192.168.200.0/24 via its eth0, which is UP). With both uplinks down, router4 has zero reachability beyond its directly connected LAN. Its RIP process still runs but self-advertises 172.25.1.0/24 and 192.168.15.0/24 at metric 16 (RIP infinity), so no routes to 172.16.10.0/24 or 172.16.20.0/24 (Location A) — nor any other remote prefix — ever enter its kernel FIB. PC11–14 send packets to their default gateway (192.168.200.1 = router4), which has no forwarding path and silently drops them.

**Localization:** The peer ends of both links are healthy — router3 eth5 (172.25.1.2) and router5 eth5 (192.168.15.1) are both UP and have full routing tables. The asymmetry confirms the failure is entirely on router4.

**Root cause:** Router4's eth4 and eth5 were deliberately brought down after startup (the startup script correctly issues `ip link set eth4 up` and `ip link set eth5 up`, but both interfaces are currently in DOWN state), completely isolating Location C from the rest of the network.

**Corrective fix:** On router4, run `ip link set eth4 up` and `ip link set eth5 up`. RIP will re-establish adjacencies with router5 and router3 within one update interval (~30 s), populate the routing table, and restore full connectivity for PC11–14 to Location A and all other zones.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router4's two uplinks—eth5 to router3 and eth4 to router5—as the affected interfaces and states they are down.
Bringing eth4 and eth5 up on router4 (ip link set eth4 up; ip link set eth5 up) matches the expected fix and will restore RIP adjacencies and routing.
